content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 5 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to output JSON tree.

We have target SMILES: O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C/C=C/C=C/C(O)=O

Looks like a polyunsaturated diol with a carboxylic acid side chain. Possibly a natural product derivative (maybe a polyunsaturated fatty acid with cyclic sugar?). Actually structure: a cyclohexane with two hydroxyls and an O-alkyl side chain containing conjugated diene and a terminal carboxylic acid (maybe a polyunsaturated fatty acid attached to a sugar). Could be a glycoside of a polyunsaturated acid.

We need retrosynthesis: break glycosidic bond (O-alkyl) to give sugar (a cyclohexane diol) and side chain (unsaturated acid). Then further break side chain maybe via olefin functionalization to simpler building blocks like acrylic acid, etc. Also sugar could be derived from simple sugar like glucose derivatives.

We need commercially available precursors. Likely we can use commercially available 1,2,3,4,5,6-hexahydroxy cyclohexane? Not sure.

Simplify: Use template 38653 which is a cyclization forming a cyclic acetal? The template transforms a linear precursor with a double bond into a cyclic ether? Actually template 38653: retro_smarts: [C:1]/[CH;D2;+0:2]=[CH;D2;+0:3]/[C:4]>>[C:1]-[C@@H;D3;+0:2]1-O-[C@H;D3;+0:3]-1-[C:4]. So forward reaction is cyclization of a diene to form a tetrahydrofuran? Actually forms a cyclic acetal: a 1,3-dioxolane? The product is a cyclic ether linking C2 and C3 via O.

Our target has a cyclic acetal? The sugar ring is a tetrahydropyran (six-membered) with O bridging? The SMILES O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]([C@@H]1C)/C=C(CO)/C)C... This is a cyclic acetal? The sugar is a 1,3-dioxane? Actually O[C@H]1C[C@@H](O[C@@H]... )C... The ring has O at position 1, and O-substituted at position 3? Might be a 1,3-dioxane.

Thus template 38653 could be used to form that cyclic ether from a linear diene precursor.

The apply_template gave two possible precursors: 
1) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO
2) C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C[C@@H]2O[C@H]2/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

These are linear precursors with a diene that cyclizes to the target.

Now we need to further break these precursors into simpler building blocks.

Let's pick the first precursor: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/[C@@H]2O[C@H]2C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

It contains a terminal alcohol (CO) and a side chain with a carboxylic acid (C(=O)O) attached to a cyclic sugar? Actually still cyclic.

Maybe we can break the glycosidic bond: O[C@@H]... The precursor still has a cyclic sugar? Actually the precursor still has the cyclic sugar (the same ring). So maybe we need a different disconnection: break the C-O bond linking the side chain to the sugar (the O-alkyl). That could be a simple ether cleavage.

Search for template that breaks an ether: maybe a SN2 substitution.

Let's search for templates that break C-O bond (ether).
